# [TASK] Identify frontend source of recent-movies data for recommendations

## Task
Identify the frontend's actual source of "recent movies" to send as
`recommendationRequest.recentMovies`.

## Scope
Audit only — no endpoint call yet. Ratings/favorites state may live in
Redux, may live purely server-side via user-service, or both; this Task
settles which one feeds the recommendations call and how it's fetched.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Existing FE state/services audited (`features/`, `services/user.js`) for where rated/favorited movies already live (no test: audit finding, see Notes)
- [x] Decision documented: which source feeds `recentMovies`, and whether it needs a new fetch or reuses an existing one (no test: audit finding, see Notes)
- [x] Empty-history case identified explicitly (new user, nothing rated/favorited yet) — this drives Task #2's empty state (no test: audit finding, see Notes)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 2

## Notes
`recentMovies` should come from Favorites only, not Watchlist: Watchlist means "not yet watched," the opposite of what a recommender needs. Favorites (`services/user.js` `getFavorites`) is the app's only "the user likes this" signal — no Redux slice duplicates it (`features/auth.js`, `features/currentGenreOrCategory.js` don't touch this state).

user-service returns only `movieId` per favorite, never a title. Task #220 needs a new step: resolve each id's title via `tmdbApi.getMovie` before building the array — the same per-id lookup `RatedCards.jsx`'s `FavoriteMovie` already does for display, just collected instead of rendered.

Empty history means `recentMovies: []`. Confirmed server-side (`RecommendationService.recommend`) this doesn't error — it drops the "recently watched" text and returns catalog-only recommendations. Task #220 should decide whether to call with `[]` or prompt the user first, mirroring the empty state `Profile.jsx` already shows for favorites/watchlist.
